hookLine: Nobody tells the man who farms the ninety-three acres.

ACT_1.primary: NINETY-THREE ACRES, BENTON AND HENRY COUNTIES
ACT_1.secondary: Fishing, farming, camping and hunting. Landlocked — reached through a neighbour's private gravel drive and gate, then a chained gate with a No Trespassing sign.

ACT_1.label: The curtilage — the narrow ring the law draws around a house

ACT_1.secondary: The second landowner — chained gates and No Trespassing signs of his own.

ACT_1.quote: He has, however, curtailed some of his usage, as he has become hesitant to use his properties or invite guests due to fear of surveillance and fear of injuring a TWRA officer.
ACT_1.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — the undisputed facts

ACT_1.quote: He fears that officers might be observing him, his girlfriend, or his guests in their private activities, and he has reduced his visits to his land, where he previously more regularly camped and fished.
ACT_1.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — Hunter Hollingsworth, the undisputed facts

ACT_1.quote: As a safety precaution, Mr. Rainwaters and his guests follow a rule that hunters should know the location of everyone else on the property.
ACT_1.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_1.label: Entries onto Rainwaters's Harmon Creek property in 2017 — photographs taken on each

ACT_1.secondary: A camera owned by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service installed on a tree on Hollingsworth's property, a branch cut to do so.

ACT_1.quote: The parties dispute whether these actions were attributable solely to federal authorities … or to both federal and state authorities.
ACT_1.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024), footnote 2 — never resolved by any court

ACT_1.primary: NO RECORDS KEPT. NO NOTICE GIVEN.
ACT_1.secondary: Officers enter private property, sometimes conceal themselves thereupon, and look for violations of wildlife laws.

lines: HOW LONG BEFORE YOU FOUND IT?

ACT_1.quote: In determining which properties to enter to investigate suspected violations of hunting laws, TWRA officers sometimes rely on having previously seen hunters on the property, on word of mouth, or on listening for shots.
ACT_1.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_1.quote: The TWRA does not impose constraints on how often a parcel is entered, what time of day an entry may be made, or how long an officer may remain on private property, and the TWRA does not have written policies for officers to follow when deciding whether to enter private property.
ACT_1.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_1.quote: The TWRA does not know how many times its agents have entered upon their properties, nor do Messrs. Rainwaters and Hollingsworth know how many times their properties were entered upon by TWRA agents.
ACT_1.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_1.label: Circuit Court for Benton County, No. 20-CV-6 — heard by a three-judge panel

ACT_1.quote: the statutory authority to go upon any property, outside of buildings, posted or otherwise, in the performance of . . . their duties to enforce wildlife laws.
ACT_1.attribution: The TWRA's characterisation of Tenn. Code Ann. § 70-1-305 — the opinion never prints it

ACT_2.secondary: the word 'possessions' was added for a purpose … refers to property, real or personal, actually possessed or occupied

ACT_2.quote: would not include wild or waste lands, or other lands that were unoccupied.
ACT_2.attribution: Welch v. State, 289 S.W. 510, 511 (Tenn. 1926), quoted in Rainwaters (2024)

ACT_2.quote: Tennessee has a robust history of protecting land outside the curtilage of a home as a 'possession' under Article I, Section 7 of the State Constitution.
ACT_2.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_2.quote: TWRA officers enter private property only when—and only in areas where— they believe hunting activity is taking place or has taken place.
ACT_2.attribution: The TWRA's reasonableness argument, quoted in Rainwaters (2024)

ACT_2.quote: It is undisputed that the TWRA believes TWRA officers have lawful authority 'to enter private property without consent or a warrant to enforce Tennessee's wildlife laws in the performance of their duties.'
ACT_2.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_2.quote: It is likewise undisputed that officers have entered the private property of others pursuant to this purported statutory authority and without consent or a warrant since the filing of this case.
ACT_2.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_2.quote: the TWRA enters upon the property of non-hunters pursuant to Tennessee Code Annotated subsections 70-1-305(1) and (7) as part of its enforcement activities.
ACT_2.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

events.text: The entry he sued over — deer baiting

ACT_2.primary: WHAT THE RECORD HOLDS OF THESE TWO MEN
ACT_2.secondary: Their land, how they used it, a girlfriend, a fear of surveillance, and a licence suspension.

items.label: Home property, two homes, farmed conspicuously
Liberty Road — fenced all the way around

ACT_2.quote: fenced all the way around, and accessible through a chained gate with 'No Trespassing signs.'
ACT_2.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — Rainwaters's 69-acre Liberty Road parcel

ACT_2.quote: the TWRA has not endeavored to defend its searches based upon any of the established exceptions to the warrant requirement.
ACT_2.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — the implied-consent theory was held waived

ACT_2.quote: the TWRA asserted at oral argument that, if the Plaintiffs wish to avoid reentry by the TWRA upon their properties, they should desist in hunting thereupon.
ACT_2.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_3.primary: COURT OF APPEALS OF TENNESSEE AT JACKSON — 9 MAY 2024
ACT_3.secondary: No. W2022-00514-COA-R3-CV. Usman, J., delivered the opinion, in which Goldin and Armstrong, JJ., joined.

ACT_3.quote: the challenger must establish that no set of circumstances exist under which the Act would be valid
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — the standard for a facial challenge

ACT_3.quote: do not dispute that the statute authorizes entries upon wild waste land areas or that such entries are constitutional under the Tennessee Constitution.
ACT_3.attribution: The plaintiffs' own concession, recorded in Rainwaters (2024)

ACT_3.quote: the statute is facially constitutional because there are applications of the statute that are constitutionally permissible.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — the trial panel's facial holding was reversed

ACT_3.quote: [a] person commits criminal trespass if the person enters or remains on property, or any portion of property, without the consent of the owner.
ACT_3.attribution: Tenn. Code Ann. § 39-14-405(a), quoted in Rainwaters (2024) — the work the entry statute does

ACT_3.quote: Their lands were secured by gates, accessible only through private drives, and posted with 'no trespassing' signs intended to limit access to them. The Plaintiffs used and occupied their land by farming, fishing, camping, and hunting.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — the as-applied finding

ACT_3.quote: While the TWRA endeavors to dismiss hunting, fishing, and camping upon one's property as recreational in nature, such activities, recreational though they may be, constitute actual use of the property.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_3.quote: We conclude that these were not wild or waste lands outside the shield of Article I, Section 7 of the Tennessee Constitution but instead 'possessions' subject to constitutional protection.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_3.quote: that general warrants, whereby an officer may be commanded to search suspected places, without evidence of the fact committed, or to seize any person or persons not named, whose offences are not particularly described and supported by evidence, are dangerous to liberty and ought not to be granted.
ACT_3.attribution: Tenn. Const. art. I, § 7 — the second half of the sentence, quoted in Rainwaters (2024)

ACT_3.quote: each agent is empowered with the discretionary authority to determine for himself or herself if there is a reasonable basis to suspect hunting activities are occurring on the property.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_3.quote: There is no clear system of judicial review that allows consideration of the TWRA's entries upon private property or their agents' comportment thereupon.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_3.quote: The TWRA searches, which it claims are reasonable, bear a marked resemblance to the arbitrary discretionary entries of customs officials more than two centuries ago in colonial Boston.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024)

ACT_3.quote: given the purpose of Article I, Section 7 of preventing arbitrary intrusions upon privacy and personal liberty, what the TWRA claims is reasonable is not.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024) — §§ 70-1-305(1) and (7), unconstitutional AS APPLIED

ACT_3.quote: The TWRA also does not articulate why reasonable suspicion rather than probable cause is the appropriate standard.
ACT_3.attribution: Rainwaters v. Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (Tenn. Ct. App. 2024), footnote 50

ACT_3.label: Nominal damages for the constitutional injury, affirmed — Ed Carter ordered to pay

ACT_3.primary: SOVEREIGN IMMUNITY — RAISED FOR THE FIRST TIME ON APPEAL
ACT_3.secondary: We conclude this argument is waived. The statute stays in the Tennessee code, facially constitutional.

ACT_4.quote: we conclude that the original meaning of the term 'possessions' as used in Article I, Section 8, unlike the term 'effects' as used in the Fourth Amendment, includes land.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) (Brobson, J.), No. 23 WAP 2023

ACT_4.quote: Open fields are afforded no constitutional protection from warrantless searches and seizure under the Fourth Amendment to the United States Constitution.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — the opinion's first sentence

ACT_4.quote: a private place—a sanctuary—where they can come to escape from the hustle and bustle of daily life.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — the undisputed record of what the membership buys

ACT_4.quote: family matters, marital problems, work stressors, romantic feelings, and faith in God.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — what members say to each other out there

ACT_4.quote: They have posted their properties' boundary lines with clearly visible 'no trespassing' signs and purple paint, installed locked gates at all public entrances, and fenced some of their properties' boundaries with waist-high, metal wire, all in an effort to exclude non-members and intruders therefrom.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026)

ACT_4.primary: THE PURPLE PAINT LAW — 18 Pa. C.S. § 3503(b)(1)(vi)
ACT_4.secondary: Pennsylvania landowners, except those in Philadelphia and Allegheny Counties, have the option to use purple paint, rather than 'no trespassing' signs, to post their properties
Warden Gritzer and other Commission officers entered the Hunting Clubs' land without consent, a warrant, or probable cause. The range is the Court's own; it is not rounded.

ACT_4.label: Days the trail camera remained on Punxsutawney's property

ACT_4.quote: Go upon any land or water outside of buildings, except curtilage, posted or otherwise, in the performance of the officer's duty.

Several Commission officers entered Russo's property, which was posted with '[n]o [t]respassing' signs, without a warrant and found several large piles of 'apple mash' as well as a corn feeder close to Russo's cabin.
ACT_4.attribution: Commonwealth v. Russo (Pa. 2007), as recounted in Punxsutawney (Pa. 2026)

ACT_4.quote: to the extent that it authorizes entry onto posted private property without any level of suspicion of illegal activity.
ACT_4.attribution: Cappy, C.J., dissenting in Russo (2007), joined by then-Justice Baer and Justice Baldwin

events.text: Commonwealth Court, en banc: bound by Russo

ACT_4.quote: slavish adherence to our decision in Russo must give way to the greater privacy and property protections afforded under Article I, Section 8 of our state charter.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026)

ACT_4.quote: the scope of the protection afforded under Article I, Section 8 to a landowner's open fields extends to private land located beyond the curtilage over which the landowner has demonstrated a reasonable and legitimate expectation of privacy by taking sufficient steps to exclude intruders therefrom.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — the rule

ACT_4.quote: we hold that stare decisis does not compel our adherence to Russo, that Russo was wrongly decided, and that Sections 303(c) and 901(a)(2) of the Code violate Article I, Section 8 of the Pennsylvania Constitution.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — the holding, under the STATE constitution

ACT_4.quote: there does not appear to be any invalid language that we can sever and that would yield operative and constitutional text consistent with the legislative intent behind the enactment of these provisions of the Code. Accordingly, the provisions fall in their entirety.
ACT_4.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026)

ACT_4.secondary: By striking Sections 303(c) and 901(a)(2) the Court had already granted the Hunting Clubs the declaratory and injunctive relief that they sought.

ACT_5.quote: We, therefore, do not discuss and/or question the federal open fields doctrine further.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026), footnote 12 — the FEDERAL doctrine is untouched

ACT_5.quote: (1) conduct warrantless searches of private property that is not posted, fenced, or otherwise marked to exclude intruders; (2) observe evidence of Code violations that occur in plain view on private property that is posted, fenced, or otherwise marked to exclude intruders;
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — what survives the ruling (1 and 2 of 4)

ACT_5.quote: (3) obtain a warrant to search private property that is posted, fenced, or otherwise marked to exclude intruders based upon their receipt of information that a Code violation has occurred; and/or
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — what survives the ruling (3 of 4)

ACT_5.quote: (4) apply a recognized exception to the warrant requirement as a means to search private property that is posted, fenced, or otherwise marked to exclude intruders.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — what survives the ruling (4 of 4)

ACT_5.secondary: Today's decision does not preclude administrative searches conducted pursuant to an appropriate statutory framework
We are not declaring that section constitutional, although it is presumptively so until a court decides otherwise.

ACT_5.quote: not a diminution of the importance of our citizens' right to the conservation, maintenance, and protection of wildlife under the ERA.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — the Environmental Rights Amendment, Pa. Const. art. I, § 27

ACT_5.quote: we cannot ignore that this case is about rural, undeveloped land, not a suburban one-acre plot or a nine-acre tract of land upon one acre in the center of which sits a swimming pool.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026), footnote 24

ACT_5.quote: There may be ways by which the owners of those latter two properties can demonstrate a reasonable and legitimate expectation of privacy that does not involve marking the boundaries of their properties with 'no trespassing' signs or purple paint.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026), footnote 24

ACT_5.quote: Truly open fields—i.e., private land that is unposted and unbounded—is fundamentally different in kind than private land conspicuously posted with 'no trespassing' signs and purple paint and/or bounded by fences, gates, and other structures.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026)

ACT_5.quote: Government officials, therefore, must obtain a warrant based upon probable cause or satisfy one of the recognized exceptions to the warrant requirement before entering the private land of any landowner that has taken such steps.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026) — under Article I, Section 8 of the STATE constitution

ACT_5.quote: we reserve for another day the question of whether the privacy protections afforded by Article I, Section 8 extend to landowners who have taken fewer steps than the Hunting Clubs, or even no steps, to exclude intruders from their properties.
ACT_5.attribution: Punxsutawney Hunting Club v. Pa. Game Commission (Pa. 2026), footnote 24

ACT_5.quote: would not include wild or waste lands, or other lands that were unoccupied.
ACT_5.attribution: Welch v. State (Tenn. 1926) — the boundary Tennessee drew a century earlier

lines: NONE OF IT WAS ON APPEAL.
emphasisWords: NONE OF IT WAS ON APPEAL

ACT_5.primary: WHAT THE TWO TENNESSEE MEN HOLD
ACT_5.secondary: A declaration that the statute was unconstitutional as applied to them. No injunction. One dollar. The statute is facially constitutional and still on the books.

ACT_5.primary: WHAT THE TWO PENNSYLVANIA CLUBS HOLD
ACT_5.secondary: Two provisions struck from the Code in their entirety, no remand, and the relief they asked for granted where they stood.

ENDING.secondary: The Pennsylvania opinion does not mention Rainwaters, Hollingsworth, or the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency.

lines: AND NOTHING TO ENFORCE IT WITH.

ENDING.primary: EACH RULING STOPS AT ITS OWN STATE LINE
ENDING.secondary: Pennsylvania decided under Article I, Section 8. Tennessee under Article I, Section 7. Neither touched the Fourth Amendment.

ENDING.primary: THE QUESTION THE WINNING COURT SET ASIDE
ENDING.secondary: Whether the protections extend to landowners who have taken fewer steps than the Hunting Clubs, or even no steps, to exclude intruders from their properties.

_readme: Provenance for figures_by_section. One entry per beat, in the same order, so a reader can check any card against EP66_openfields_FACTS_LEDGER.v001.md. ledger_rows are the ledger row ids behind every factual assertion on that card; lands_on is the measured narration the beat sits over, from 06_audio/narration_index.v001.json. Nothing here is read by any tool.

PLACEMENT. build_case_film_generic.build_figures() does not read a per-beat time: it spaces a section's payloads EVENLY inside the section window (dur 6.0s, and 3.0s in HOOK/OP), reserving 3.0s at the head and 6.5s at the tail. The ORDER and the COUNT are therefore the only placement controls, and both were chosen against the measured narration rather than against the paper design. Every beat was verified to overlap the narration chunk it illustrates.

BEAT COUNTS. episode_spec figure_beats_per_act is [13,17]. ACT_1-ACT_4 carry 17, the ceiling. ACT_5 carries 16, not 17: at 17 the grid put a card across the designed 5s hold after footnote 24 (the recognition) and left PA-35 with no beat; 16 fixes both and is still high in the band. HOOK 3, OP 1, ENDING 8 -- those three are not acts and the floor does not apply to them.

SACRIFICIAL SLOTS. build_figures overwrites figures[0] and figures[-1] with the AI-disclosure lowerthird. HOOK[0] and ENDING[-1] are therefore already that card, so no content beat is destroyed. EP65's v001 lost its closing line this way.

NO acttitle CARDS, deliberately. EP62-65 open each act with one. Here every slot is spoken for, and ACT_4 in particular opens on the scripted hard cut -- place, date, PA-25, 'Includes land.', 'We hereby overrule Russo.' with no connective word (script v003 line 394). A title card there is a connective. Structure is carried by the opening card of each act instead.

FEDERAL vs STATE. Every card that states a holding names the constitution it rests on. ACT_5[0] (PA-36 / ND-04) and ENDING[5] (ND-12) exist only to hold the two levels apart. No card says either court touched the Fourth Amendment.

NUMBERS. The only numerals asserted are 3 (TN-11), 136 and 69 (TN-09), $1 (TN-40), 78 (PA-13), the constitution years (TN-24) and the docket dates. The 15-22 range is written as a range in prose (PA-12, open question -06), never as a ticker. No percentage, acreage or count of landowners/cameras/entries/states/agencies appears anywhere; the 96% figure is banned outright (ledger -06).

KNOWN PLACEMENT LIMIT -- ACT_2[16], the TN-19 line ('they should desist in hunting thereupon'). build_figures reserves the last 6.5s of every section, so no beat can start after 579.4s; the line is spoken 582.8-590.1. The card therefore reads 575.6-581.6, i.e. while the narrator introduces the quotation, and leaves 1.2s before he delivers it. Changing the beat count does not move it -- the last slot is always centred in the final interval. Accepted, and recorded rather than hidden.

LEDGER ROWS SPOKEN BUT NOT GIVEN A CARD (the grid has fewer slots than the script has lines): TN-05 (officers cross land not under investigation), TN-18, PA-01 (4,400 and 1,100 acres), PA-05, PA-14, PA-26, PA-32, PC-05, TN-41 and the Pennsylvania vote split (deliberately -- quarantine -10 forbids characterising it). All are narrated; none is contradicted.

_declared_values.leadSeconds: 0 -- SPEC v2 row 9, binding from EP66: the hook is VOICED from frame 0, so the body sequence and the <Audio> master inside it start at the first frame and there is no silent lead. Absent, every consumer computes hookSeconds + OPENING_SEC (11.5 s), which is what EP62-65 use; the key is opt-in and this is the first episode to declare it.
_declared_values.openingVariant: 'overlay' -- EP66_openfields_PACKAGING.v001.md sections 4 and 7. With a zero lead there is no room in front of the body for the full-screen 3.5 s brand card, so <BrandOpening> renders in its lower-band form OVER the running cut and the running narration. Without this key the film would carry NO channel opening at all; scripts/build_case_film_generic.py now refuses to build that combination and check_final_acceptance.check_bookends() now fails it.
_declared_values.hookSeconds: 19.468 -- MEASURED, from episodes/PD-2026-066-openfields/06_audio/narration_index.v001.json after the 2026-08-10 hook extension: the HOOK section runs VC-0001 0.000 -> VC-0008 19.468. This is no longer a design figure. HISTORY, so nobody re-derives it: PACKAGING section 3 designed a 20.3 s picture window, but the first delivered master read the HOOK in 13.295 s, which put the brand band (hookSeconds + CaseFilm.OPENING_OVERLAY_OFFSET_SEC 0.2 = 20.5) four seconds inside ACT_1 and left the first twenty seconds with no statement of what the film is about. The owner requirement -- the first twenty seconds must say what the film is, what the payoff is and what the viewer gets -- was met by ADDING two lines to the HOOK (+16 narration words, +100 characters, 2 new voice chunks VC-0006/VC-0007), not by moving a number. The re-measured master runs HOOK 0.000-19.468, OP 21.268-22.522, ACT_1 from 24.322. WHERE THE BAND LANDS NOW: 19.468 + 0.2 = 19.668, held for Bookends.OPENING_SEC 3.5 s, so it falls at 23.168 -- up for the whole of the recorded OP line (Nobody has to., 21.268-22.522) and gone 1.15 s before ACT_1 speaks. That is PACKAGING section 3 own stated intent (its 0:20.7-0:21.8 row puts the overlay rise against that line on the empty field) reached 0.8 s earlier than the paper design -- not a new intent. PACKAGING sections 3/4/7 still print 20.3 / 20.5 / 24.0; those three numbers are now 0.8-1.0 s stale and want a PACKAGING v002. NOT edited here: it is an approved front document. structure_4part requires hookSeconds >= HOOK_MIN_SEC 5.0, and 19.468 passes.
_declared_values.hookLine: Verbatim, the closing line of the HOOK section of episodes/_planning/EP66_openfields_script.en.v003.md (also VC-0006 of narration_index.v001.json). PACKAGING section 4.4 defines hookLine as the cold open's closing line. It is not drawn on screen in the overlay layout -- the Hook montage sequence does not render at a zero lead -- but structure_4part requires it to be non-empty and it is the film's declaration of what the cold open ends on.
_declared_values.captionLeadSeconds: 0.0 -- the captions in 08_edit/captions.final.v001.srt were already aligned with the house 0.60 s lead (out_ep66_captions.log: 'applied caption lead -0.60s'). scripts/_finish_episode.sh step 4b re-polishes the srt and used to hard-code --lead 0.25, which would have pushed EP66 to 0.85 s. That step now reads this key and falls back to 0.25 when it is absent, so EP62-65 are unaffected.
